Not Quite "Anime Dark Souls"

I really wanted to love Code Vein, but it constantly feels like it’s fighting against itself. Coming to this right after playing The First Berserker: Khazan made those flaws stand out even more—Khazan executed this exact anime Souls-like style so much better.

Here is why Code Vein drags the experience down by comparison:

Where do I go? The level design gets super frustrating. Maps (especially the infamous Cathedral) are mazes of copy-pasted corridors with almost zero visual landmarks to guide you.

Confusing UI: The interface is cluttered, and the item icons all look almost identical. You’ll find yourself constantly opening sub-menus just to figure out what you picked up.

Floaty Combat: Fights lack that heavy, satisfying punch, and there isn’t much room for cool combo chains—it’s mostly just single swing, roll, wait for cooldowns, repeat.

If you're a big fan of the aesthetic or love playing with an AI companion, you might still have some fun on sale! But if you want tight combat and great exploration, go play Khazan instead.

I've been having a great time playing this game. The gameplay is fun, the world is interesting to explore, and it's one of those games that keeps making me want to play "just a little longer." Before I know it, hours have already passed.

My only real struggle is during the early stages when the map hasn't been fully unlocked yet. I often find myself getting lost, running in circles, or spending more time figuring out where to go than actually completing objectives. It can be a little confusing at times, especially in larger areas.

That said, once I start learning the layout and unlocking more of the map, exploration becomes much more enjoyable. Despite occasionally getting lost, the overall experience is still very entertaining and rewarding. If you enjoy exploring and discovering things on your own, you'll probably have a lot of fun with this game.

Overall, I definitely recommend it. Just be prepared to get lost a few times before the map opens up.

Code Vein is an anime-inspired action RPG that borrows many ideas from the Soulslike genre while adding its own twists. It features challenging combat, deep character customization, and a strong emphasis on companions. While it doesn't quite reach the heights of the best games in the genre, it's an excellent choice for fans of anime and action RPGs.

What it does well
Flexible build system. Instead of locking you into a class, the Blood Code system lets you switch roles at any time. You can easily experiment with different weapons, spells, and abilities without restarting the game.
Excellent character creator. One of the most detailed character creators in the genre, allowing players to design highly customized protagonists.
Fun combat. Battles are fast and rewarding, combining melee attacks, dodges, parries, and powerful "Gifts" (special abilities).
AI companions. Unlike many Soulslikes, you can bring a partner who helps in combat, revives you, and makes the game more approachable.
Strong soundtrack and anime presentation. The visual style and music complement the game's dark, post-apocalyptic atmosphere.
Weaknesses
Level design is inconsistent. Some areas are memorable, while others—especially the infamous Cathedral—can be confusing and repetitive.
Storytelling is uneven. The narrative has emotional moments, but some characters and plot points don't receive enough development.
Enemy variety. You'll encounter repeated enemy types throughout much of the adventure.
Gameplay

Combat rewards careful timing and resource management. Key features include:

Switching Blood Codes to change your playstyle instantly.
Customizing Gifts for melee, ranged, or magic-focused builds.
Choosing between one-handed swords, greatswords, hammers, halberds, and bayonets.
Exploring interconnected environments filled with shortcuts, secrets, and challenging bosses.

The companion system makes solo play more forgiving, though experienced players can disable companions fo…

I like everything about this game, except:
- can't pause cutscenes when something comes during playtime, your best chance is to skip them and search "code vein all cutscenes" on YouTube and pick up from there
- newer CPUs (13th and 14th gen) require entering BIOS and disabling Hyper-threading/E-cores, otherwise you'll gonna have to wait 10-15 min for each launch of the game
- not enough customization options, at least clothes-wise, for now only fixable with mods

All I've just mentioned could easily be fixed with a patch + DLC, but from what I saw, this game is kinda abandonware now. Still good, still worth playing, but you gotta know these first, if you're looking for the "perfect experience".

Also this > the Tokyo Ghoul game in any aspect, same publisher, similar aesthetics/ atmosphere/ themes, had to mention it for the edgy anime fans.

While I'm generally a lot more constructive in my feedback for games, I'll put in the same effort the developers did into making the combat encounters with the same three enemies you fight repeatedly through copy and pasted environments. This game is bad. It's advertisement tagline "It's anime Dark Souls" is such a gross misunderstanding of what makes any Souls-adjacent title great it saddens me that so many parrot that exact tagline. 

Additionally, If you happen to have a 13th or 14th gen Intel processor like I do, you also have to wait ~10 minutes when you hit play on Steam for the game to actually launch thanks to its failure to utilize hyperthreading appropriately. The only alternative solution is to disable HT in your BIOS. I doubt I'd perform that for my favorite game let alone one I actively didn't enjoy.

For those not familiar with soulslikes and being attracted by the anime aesthetic, its important to warn you that , in stark contrast to the OG Series, the really bad hitboxes and stunlock patterns on some enemies are by far the worst part of the game. I can see newcomers becoming very frustrated by them, getting 'stuck' and thinking its normal for the genre (its not). My advice is to early on use Iron Will/Shifting Hollow/(Yakumo's) Foulblood Barrier to get you through the starter zones until you can set up a Quick roll loadout and it should be smooth sailing from there.

The DLC's only add (very short) post-game dungeons with mainly re-used bosses and can be safely skipped.

Combat 7.5/10

Story 5/10 
-Just watch a movie instead. I found with how much info they throw at you I just lost interest. 
Content 8.5/10
-Could easily have been a 10 but there just isn't enough true enemy variety. Oh you liked red guy? Here's red guy but blue. The DLC should be the saving grace as in theory it's a lot of content, until you realise it's just fighting the same boss over and over again. That being said, you can play this game for hundreds of hours if you do enjoy it. 

Overall 7/10. If you enjoy souls games, you'll enjoy this one. For anyone else, I can't recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight the extensive character creator and flexible build system utilizing Blood Codes and transferable gifts.

citations.review_text:
I've had this game on my radar and wanted to play it for years, but I only just managed to complete it now. Compared to other Souls-like games, it's a very good game; I'd say it's around tier A of the Souls-like games I've finished. I liked almost everything about it. 

- Combat - Very fluid and largely dependent on your build. I think combat is the most important thing in this game, if not for one small thing.

- Story - Finally, there's a specific story in this type of game; its presence and level alone make it superior to other Soulslike games.

- characters - Our team is made up of very interesting characters, and it's great that we always take one person into battle.

- Character Development - There are a lot of classes and weapons, so you can create virtually any build.

- Regions and Exploration - Navigating the maps is very enjoyable, and solid exploration is rewarded with various collectibles.

- Difficulty Level - Usually, the map battles are at an appropriate level; they're demanding, requiring focus, but generally, the battles are at a good difficulty level. As for the bosses, they're at a standard level for this series; most bosses are around 5-15 attempts, and a few of the hardest ones take about 30 attempts. There are a few walls, and you have to be patient, but I expected there would be obstacles, and there were.

NEGATIVES:
- Silent protagonist - I will never accept this, and it will always be a minus for me, especially in a story-heavy game like this.

Small minus:
- It's very easy to get staggered while fighting, which forces a specific combat style because enemy hits can lead to a combo where you stand still and take damage. We also stagger quite easily, and on the one hand, it's too easy.

A very, very weird ([i]not[/i] in a good or interesting way) and problematic soulslike. Three key things contribute to this.

First, the game is balanced around having a Companion but is, strangely, far too easy with a Companion. Without a Companion, since the game is actively balanced around having one, the game is needlessly difficult due to mechanics built with having a Companion out in mind. Companion effectiveness is also tied to level, which means Companions can come close to playing for the player [i]rather than[/i] enabling build variety (e.g. healer build).

Second, progression is just incredibly weird and arbitrary due to how stats, gear upgrades, and Gifts (abilities) work. (Plug Companion effectiveness into this and it gets weirder and more arbitrary.) Stats are directly tied to Blood Codes and gear, first, and level, second. While this makes switching between build ideas completely seamless, players have to already have the Gifts to make that viable. When it comes down to it, upgrades don't really feel like much of an upgrade due to the presence of Companions.

Third, Gift unlocking is, again, incredibly weird. Gifts are first tied to Blood Codes where they can be unlocked and equipped. After mastering them by getting enough experience through enemy interactions/kills, the player can use a mastered Gift with another Blood Code as long as it meets the minimum requirements. In practise, this means that the player will be regularly switching out builds to unlock skills -some are vital for certain areas (like curing poison), some are next to useless, and some genuinely help with a player's build.

And, as a final bit, the 'good ending' makes the narrative incoherent in a way that would make FromSoftware blush. It's all just very, very weird.

Code Vein will forever hold a special place in my heart as this is the game that got me to finally dive deep into the Soulsborne/SoulsLike genre, and I have not looked back since.

The game is more on the faster side and some of the enemies are very fast as well. 

Two major differences in this game compared to other Souls games are the way you level up and a partner you get to have.

***Spoilers***

Leveling-Up:
[spoiler]Leveling up is not done in the traditional way. When you level up you do so as a whole. Your Strength, Dex, Vit etc, all level up together. This is where the Blood Codes come in. That is your main way of using your weapons, armors and Gifts (magic)[/spoiler]

Partner:
[spoiler]You can use one of multiple partners and it depends on your style of play. If you go full tank, then you might want someone more agile. If you focus more on agility/dex then Yakumo might be best since he is a tank and deals HUGE damage. Having him as a partner definitely makes things easier so if you want more of a challenge you might want someone else[/spoiler]

Story:
[spoiler]Without giving too much away - If you go straight through the game the story can seem meh to ok. To really get the full background of everyone and what happened, make sure to look at all the vestiges possible[/spoiler]

All in all it was fun and me being a huge Vampire and Anime fan, this was right down my alley.

Had a really fun time playing CODE VEIN. It mixes challenging combat with great customization and a cool anime-style atmosphere.

• Fast and satisfying combat
• Great character customization
• Awesome visuals and soundtrack
• Flexible build system with Blood Codes
• Fun and memorable boss fights
• Companion system makes solo play more enjoyable

Definitely worth checking out if you enjoy Souls-like RPGs.

Hmm..... ok, ok. I'll give this a [b]POSITIVE[/b].

But...
BUT....

[b]BUUUUUUUUUT!!![/b]


The cathedral is one of THE single worst designed maps in gaming. Blighttown seems bad, but it's actually cleverly designed. 4-2 (Demon's Souls) is pretty bad, but at least you can more or less sprint through the main path without confusing turns and branching paths. Water temple (OoT) is bad, but comparatively manageable.

The cathedral is essentially Anor Londo, but where every-f**kin-corner and drop loops into a different path, that branches into 3 more paths, that further has 2 more drops and a ladder at the end of it. It's awful. Legitimately awful design. It's just a confusing mess of drops, t-sections and ladders that make no sense at all.

There's a "quick cathedral guide" on Youtube, and it's the quickest I've managed to find; it's [b]17[/b] minutes long. In comparison, Anor Londo's "quick guide" is 5:50.

This one area is why I dropped the game several years ago, and why I'm now picking it back up again, but going through this god-awful area using a guide.


That aside, it's ok. Even fun-ish? I wish there were more weapon type options, but even in the same weapon class movesets can differ, so it keeps it interesting enough. Magic is a viable option, too, as is ranged. Decent enough game; phenomenal customization.


Do NOT pay full price though. It's not worth $70-80 (not even close). Wait for a hefty 60~90% off.


EDIT: already got bored of it after playing for like 6 hours. It's an easy game to get bored of. Enemies, locations, all seem kinda samey after a while.
fun game, but its the story is mid as hell. The church is pretty terrible, but after that, exploration is more doable. try to get this on discount y'all

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the DLC content as underwhelming and a waste of money, offering reused elite enemies, unique bosses with difficult challenges, and companion alternative skins.

citations.review_text:
Well, you can call it anime soulslike.
Character customization is limited, but okayish.

story is okay and interesting a little.

Gameplay wise, it is not as simple as it looks but gameplay challenges are mixed between easy and frustrating.
fighting mechanics is okayish and weird, but does the job. The bloodcode mechanic (character class) is very interesting, you can switch, mix & match to your liking (some restrictions apply) on skills and perks to build your ultimate skillsets.

DLCs is basically waste of money, unless you wanna fight broken elites(same as vanilla game but over-leveled) and unique area bosses with stupid challenges to get their blood code, some alternative skins (i think 3) for each of your companion, some "uinique" weapons (basically vanilla weapon with built in element infusion)

overall, it's not a bad game. it had interesting ideas but not the perfect way to execute them.
If it interests you, buy it on sales.

As someone who has beaten the game twice with two different endings and bought the dlc, I just wanna say that Code Vein is more like Code Depression. Just wanted to say that I love the art style and the characters, especially Io. The customization is so diverse and the story is just full of suffering.
​But the main issue is the combat. Sometimes when I try to attack using M1, it doesn't even react. And when you press parry, the animation takes so long, you literally have to wait for the parry animation to finish before you can dodge. Somehow, during an attack, it suddenly swings in a completely different direction even though I've already locked onto the enemy. The cutscenes are pretty predictable, but honestly they really need to rethink the DLC because it's pretty underwhelming, and they definitely need to fix that combat.

​If you guys want to buy this game, you should wait for a 75% sale or above. It's totally worth it at that price point, and it's actually a great price to pick the game up. I still recommend this game anyway.

One of my most favorite games! I played this game 4 times and got all 4 endings plus the DLC! This action vampiric soulslike design of a game was different than most very bloody.

The gameplay: has a lot of Blood Codes (classes) and after mastering some of the abilities you can equip them to other Blood Codes changing your play style completely. (Queenslayer) was the one I used like 95% of time.

The partner system: I used and it was something that other soulslike games didn't do. It saved me so many times in boss fights of them saving me or me saving them. (throwing around a little piece of health in those dire situations when your out of healing).

The story: I feel like they did a good job telling the story as you uncover the mysteries of the world and what's going on as you play through the game story. You kind get thrown in there. But definitely cried at certain parts.(definitely picks up at the end of the Cathedral)

The Characters: the team and the ones at home base, your friends, interacting is some of the most wholesome moments and finding vestiges (which also unlocks class abilities) you can learn about their pass lives and it gives us more about the character or characters.

The DLC: I feel like it was okay, but it definitely gives Jack more of a past and story which he needed.

I recommend trying this game out!

citations.review_text: Code Vein is a solid anime-inspired soulslike that combines challenging combat with flexible character builds through its Blood Code system. The Steam version runs well overall, with smooth performance and stable gameplay, while the art style and soundtrack create a memorable atmosphere. Boss fights are enjoyable, character customization is excellent, and the companion system makes the experience more accessible without removing the challenge. The Cathedral can be confusing to navigate, but overall Code Vein delivers a rewarding adventure for both soulslike fans and newcomers alike.

Code Vein has a soft spot in my heart despite it's many flaws; outside the reused enemy models, music tracks, and attack patterns, tedious or downright confusing and labyrinthian level design, the skeleton that this game was built on, that is to say:

It's build system and customizable playstyles that come attached to it are extremely polished and well put together, and the story at least had my attention consistently, and the character creation is very fun and well designed. it was overall very rewarding to finish.

7.5/10, worth if on sale.

Although this game is a "Souls-like," it isn't quite as punishing or difficult as the classic titles in the genre. I say this as someone who isn't typically a fan of Souls games, yet managed to complete this one four times—earning the Platinum trophy—with very few issues (perhaps only a couple of bosses proved genuinely challenging). 

The game boasts a wonderful atmosphere and features companions who are both interesting and diverse. The overarching lore of the universe is a bit questionable in places, but it remains engaging enough to keep you playing. I enjoy the build-crafting system, even if some of its elements feel a bit dubious; for instance, I ended up with a massive surplus of resources that I never actually used in combat (while some resources *are* meant to be used in battle, their impact is so negligible—or so fleeting—that I barely touched them at all). 

A special "tip of the hat" goes to one particular area—the Cathedral of the Sacred Blood—after which I seriously thought I was losing my mind and would need to check myself into a hospital for psychiatric treatment (by this maze exploration). Yet, here I am on the other side, and I can say the game is wonderful—provided you enjoy anime aesthetics, deep lore, and a somewhat more forgiving approach to gameplay mechanics. It’s not bad; it just could have been better. 

I highly recommend this game if you’re looking for a moderate Souls-like experience without the usual soul-crushing suffering; if you enjoy vampire-themed stories about returning to life to atone for past mistakes; and if you’re simply curious to see how the narrative concludes—especially since there are three distinct endings. 

I also have a quick tip for achievement hunters: the "Exalted Reputation" achievement requires an immense amount of grinding if you don't have a partner to play with. Furthermore—speaking from my own personal experience—playing through the game with a friend proved to be quite tedious, as the progression system is…

I have played this game 3 times over and I absolutely love it but ♥♥♥♥ the White Castle bit I keep getting lost. other then that good fights, maps, and a very good story 100/10 would souls like again (edit I got lost 2 more times... idk how I just did)

One of the best I've played so far, this game has a lot of variety of blood codes (classes). It's up to the player to find their style of combat choices. 

As for the cutscene, it feels a bit wonky, but I enjoy my time learning the lore of the story. Aside from that, the map feels loopy especially the Cathedral map got me loopy for around an hour. I recommend trying this game out!

"anime soulslike" as they call it. each of the words can either draw some people to or turn off some from trying the game. id say the difficulty depends on your understanding of the game mechanics, at least thats how my first 20hrs went. i didnt understand some of it at first and i had HUGE struggle on the 2nd boss and even some mid-late bosses are straight bulsht and not satisfying to beat. i continuously learning throughout the game as admitedly im not smart as those internet guide dudes. i still have no idea about best builds aside from those that proved to work n i enjoy using. also i love that i can mix matching weapons, classes and skills on the fly. huge plus for customizability and replayability, sometimes i find myself swapping skills and equipments just for the sake of trying to "look cool" or "out of a anime or movie"

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features an NPC companion system that assists in combat, revives the player, and makes the game more forgiving than traditional soulslike titles.

citations.review_text:
It's not the best Souls-like game, and it does have its flaws, but it is still very fun and enjoyable. It does have familiar elements like hidden passages and dropdown points, shortcuts, traps, etc. The majority of the game world can be travelled without any cutscenes or warping, but it isn't interconnected in the way DS1 is, rather it's more like the first half of DS2, but that's not a bad thing imo. 

The combat is probably the biggest selling point since it really takes skills (abilities) to the next level. The weapon variety is relatively small, but has a bit of a quality over quantity feel to it, most weapons within their respective classes feeling pretty distinct. My personal favorite weapons being the Bayonet Rifles because GUN. Though, they can't be free aimed like DS bows, which is the one complaint I have with them. Like, I see a cheeky bastard hanging on the ceiling thinking he's all sneaky, but the game wouldn't let me lock on to them. It would be nice to at least be able to free aim in those instances.

The game does have a bit of a focus on having NPC companions, and definitely feels balanced around that due to the number of ganks there are. Plus, a number of some of the really good skills are unique to specific NPCs. You can play without NPCs, but I don't think that's really the intended experience, so keep that in mind.

I also really like the level up system. Instead of the traditional stat allocation system, leveling up only increase the player character's base HP and Attack Rating, and to meet requirements, we instead have the "Blood Code" system, which is essentially a class system that can be changed at any time in the game, which I find pretty neat and comes with their own perks (basically rings from DS) and skills. Sure, you might not get to make your own super broken, perfectly optimized build, but respecing is completely free and can be done literally whenever you want.

The story is nothing really special, the characters are a littl…
